name: Venetian Arsenal, First Factory System
summary: Venice's Arsenal employs 2,000 workers in an assembly-line production system, producing a galley per day at peak production in the early 16th century. The Arsenal's innovation: standardized parts, sequential assembly, specialized workers, and state management of production. Visiting dignitaries (including Henry III of France) are shown the Arsenal as a demonstration of Venetian state power, a complete galley launched during dinner.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Venetian Arsenal is the first industrial facility in history, its assembly-line production, standardized components, and state management anticipate the 19th-century factory system by 400 years; the Arsenal's capacity to rapidly produce a war fleet is the military foundation of Venetian naval dominance; its organizational principles (standardization, specialization, sequential production) are the conceptual ancestors of modern manufacturing
